chunks: He who is sorrowful for this world is in fact displeased with the dispensation of Allāh. He who complains of a calamity that befalls him complains of his Lord (Allāh). He who approaches a rich man and bends before him on account of his riches then two-third of his religion is gone. If a man reads the Qur’ān and on dying goes to Hell then it means that he was among those who treated Divine verses with mockery. If a man’s heart gets attached to the world, then it catches three things, namely worry that never leaves him, greed that does not abandon him and desire which he never fulfils.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual consequences of being attached to the world and complaining about divine decree?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) synthesizes the internal state of the believer with external actions, linking sorrow over worldly loss directly to *al-kurh bi qada' Allah* (displeasure with divine decree), a concept central to Shia theology regarding *rida* (contentment). The warning against excessive humility before the wealthy reflects the scholarly distinction between *tawadu'* (true modesty) and *tadhallul* (self-abasement), which erodes spiritual dignity. Furthermore, the hadith connects superficial Quranic recitation to the fate of those who made divine signs a mockery, emphasizing that true engagement requires moving beyond mere recitation to internalization.
